description: Medical documents from the clinic — intake forms, triage tags, treatment notes, medication logs, quarantine instructions, dose ledgers, autopsy reports, nurse's notes, physician's reports. Tone depends on author: the nurse's note differs from the physician's report. No gore for spectacle. The horror is in the margin.

cases.symptoms: Walked in unaided. Nausea, two emeses on arrival. Scalp hair pulling free with gentle traction. Petechiae on forearms, no external bleeding. Lymph nodes not palpable. Oriented, frightened.
cases.intervention: Oral fluids, small and frequent. Prussian blue slurry 3g if available. Isolate from drafts. Nothing by mouth for the next hour, then broth.
cases.doctor_margin_note: He asked if the sky would be blue again. I did not answer. I am the intake nurse. I take the pulse and the name. The sky is not my department. I wrote his name twice because the first time my hand shook.

cases.symptoms: Retrieved from the river, coughing. Wet rales bilaterally. Temperature 38.2. Cannot give history — does not speak the common tongue or will not. No external trauma. Clothes saturated, cold.
cases.intervention: Dry clothing from stores. Warm by the stove, rotated. Hot broth, sips. Watch for the cough.
cases.doctor_margin_note: She was blue when they brought her, the cold-blue, not the sick-blue. I could not tell which at first. She is the sick-blue now. I do not know her name. I wrote 'river woman' on the form. The form wants a name. The river is the name I have.

cases.symptoms: Burn to the right hand and forearm, scald, from the kettle. Blistering, second degree, no char. Hand function intact. Child is quiet, too quiet, did not cry on cleaning.
cases.intervention: Cool clean water flush (done). Honey dressing if available, else clean cloth and boiled-water-soaked linen. Elevate. Watch for infection.
cases.doctor_margin_note: He did not cry. Children who do not cry are the children who worry me. The children who cry are the children who are still asking. Kolya is not asking. I do not know what Kolya is doing. I dressed his hand and I sang the song and he did not cry and I cried and he did not see me cry because I am the nurse and the nurse does not cry in front of the child.

cases.symptoms: Walked in with the family, 7 persons. Elder female, ambulatory, mild dehydration. Joint pain (chronic, pre-existing). No acute complaint. Says she is here to 'see the school'.
cases.intervention: Fluids. Rest. No acute intervention indicated.
cases.doctor_margin_note: She asked where the school was. I said the clinic is not the school. She said the school is where the teacher is and the teacher is here and so the school is here. I did not argue. The form does not have a field for the school. The form has a field for the complaint. The complaint is the school. I wrote 'school' in the complaint field. The form is the form.

cases.symptoms: 14 persons presented following the storm. 4 respiratory (ash inhalation), 3 lacerations (flying debris), 2 fractures (1 rib, 1 wrist), 1 hypothermia, 4 minor/walking wounded.
cases.intervention: Triage by category: RED — rib fracture (elderly), hypothermia. YELLOW — 2 lacerations requiring suture, wrist fracture. GREEN — 4 minor, respiratory mild. BLACK — none today.
cases.outcome: All processed. 2 admitted (RED). 5 treated and released (YELLOW). 7 walking (GREEN).
cases.doctor_margin_note: No black tags today. I am grateful for the no black tags. The gratitude is unprofessional. The professional is the count. The count is 14 and 0. I am writing the 0 in the margin because the form does not have a field for the 0 and the 0 is the thing I am grateful for and the form does not have a field for gratitude.

cases.symptoms: 9 persons presented with nausea, emesis, cramping within 4h of the midday meal. Common meal: barley soup. Suspected contamination (flour or water).
cases.intervention: Triage: all GREEN. Fluids, rest, charcoal if available. Isolate the remaining soup batch. Quartermaster notified.
cases.outcome: All recovered within 24h. Soup batch isolated and destroyed.
cases.doctor_margin_note: The flour. I did not write 'the flour' on the tag. I wrote 'suspected contamination.' The flour is the suspicion. The suspicion is not the tag. The tag is the count. The count is 9 and 0. The flour is the margin. The margin is where the doctor writes what the doctor suspects. The doctor suspects the flour. The doctor does not write the flour on the tag because the tag is the tag and the flour is the flour and the two are different documents.

cases.symptoms: Day 12. Wet cough persists. Rales right lower lobe. Temperature 38.4 (up from 38.2). Sputum now purulent. No hemoptysis.
cases.intervention: Begin broad-spectrum, oral, 1 course. Continue fluids. Move to sheeted bay for isolation pending second case.
cases.doctor_margin_note: I am starting the broad. I have fourteen. I will have thirteen. The broad is for what may be a narrow and I cannot culture it. I am guessing. A doctor who guesses writes it down. I am writing it down. I am guessing.

cases.symptoms: Day 19. Cough unchanged. Temperature 38.6. Rales now bilaterally. Second case presenting identical symptoms (the man who carried her, see case med_treat_09). Contagion suspected.
cases.intervention: Transfer to clinic sheeted bay (see Transfer Order). Continue broad. Begin isolation protocol. Sheet is the barrier we have.
cases.doctor_margin_note: The sheet is not a wall. The sheet is what we have. I am writing 'the sheet is what we have' in every note until I have a wall. I do not have a wall. I have a sheet. The sheet is the medicine. The sheet is the policy. I am the policy.

cases.symptoms: Day 19. The man who carried the river woman from the river. Strong, adult, previously well. Now: wet cough, temperature 38.3, rales right lower lobe. Identical presentation to case med_treat_07.
cases.intervention: Begin broad-spectrum, oral. Isolate (sheeted bay, with case med_treat_07).
cases.doctor_margin_note: He carried her. He carried her from the river and now he has what she has. He is the strongest of us and he has what she has. I do not know if he gave it to her or she gave it to him or the river gave it to both. The river is the patient I am not treating. The river is the patient I cannot treat.

cases.symptoms: Day 14. Burn healing clean. No infection. Granulation good. Hand function intact, full range. Child eating well, sleeping well.
cases.intervention: Continue honey dressing, changed daily. No further intervention indicated.
cases.outcome: Healing. Will discharge to ward when epithelialized.
cases.doctor_margin_note: He is healing. The children who do not cry heal the fastest, or the slowest, I do not know which. He is healing. That is the word. I am writing the word. The word is the medicine today.

cases.symptoms: Broad-spectrum (type A, oral), course 1 of 2 approved. Day 1.
cases.intervention: Administered: 1 dose, morning, with broth. Tolerated. No emesis.
cases.doctor_margin_note: I gave her the first pill. I have thirteen now. The twelve is tomorrow. The eleven is the day after. The number is the number. I am counting the pills and the pills are the patients and the patients are the number. The number is going down. The patients are not all going up.

cases.symptoms: Broad-spectrum (type A, oral), course 2 of 2 approved (see Requisition). Day 1.
cases.intervention: Administered: 1 dose, morning. Tolerated.
cases.doctor_margin_note: The second course. I have eleven now. I held the third in reserve per standing order. The reserve is the reserve. The reserve is the number I do not give. The number I give is going down. The number I do not give is staying. The staying is the reserve. The reserve is the doctor's. The doctor holds the reserve. I hold the pill. The pill is the patient. The reserve is the doctor.

cases.symptoms: Potassium iodide, prophylactic, single dose, shelter-wide. Day 9 post-event (delayed, supply arrival Day 8).
cases.intervention: Administered to 140 persons (headcount Day 9). 7 persons (Loma family) not yet present — to receive on arrival. Children dosed by weight. No adverse reactions.
cases.doctor_margin_note: The iodine is late. The iodine should have been Day 1. The iodine was Day 9. The thyroid does not care about the supply chain. The thyroid cares about the iodine. I gave the iodine. I gave it late. I am writing 'late' in the margin because the form wants the dose and the dose is the dose and the lateness is the margin. The margin is where the nurse writes what the nurse cannot fix. I cannot fix the lateness. I gave the iodine.

cases.symptoms: Two cases, consistent presentation, possible contagion. Ward B under quarantine pending clinical outcome. Culturing unavailable.
cases.intervention: No entry except medical and Duty Clerk (supervised). No exit except medical transfer. Meals at the door. Water delivered, not at the public pump. Duration: until lifted by physician.
cases.doctor_margin_note: The sheet is not a wall. I have written this before. I will write it again. The quarantine is the sheet. The sheet is the policy. I am the policy. The policy is in the margin. The margin is where the doctor lives. The doctor lives in the margin because the form does not have a field for the policy and the policy is the doctor and the doctor is the margin.

cases.symptoms: Black mold growth, sub-level 3, reported by maintenance (see Inspection 14-AF). Two stock-pickers with respiratory complaints (mild, cough, not the Ward B pattern).
cases.intervention: Restrict sub-level 3 to essential access only. Respirator or damp cloth for all entries. No eating or drinking in sub-level 3. Mold remediation: deferred (no effective agent available). Monitor stock-pickers.
cases.outcome: In effect. Two complaints, mild, resolving.
cases.doctor_margin_note: The mold is the building. The building is the mold. We are treating the building with the same protocol we treat the people: restrict, cover the face, do not eat near it. The building is the patient. The building is the patient I cannot cure. I can only tell people to cover their faces near it. The face is the medicine. The medicine is a cloth. We are a clinic of cloths.

cases.symptoms: Day 30. Acute exposure Day 1 (4200 mSv estimated). Chronic follow-up. Persistent epilation. Lymphocyte count 0.4 (improved from 0.1). Petechiae resolved. Fatigue, persistent. Weight loss, 6kg.
cases.intervention: Continue supportive care. Prussian blue course complete. No further chelation indicated. Rest. Nutrition as available.
cases.outcome: Survived acute phase. Chronic marrow depression. Prognosis: guarded long-term.
cases.doctor_margin_note: He is alive. The 4200 should have killed him. He is alive. I do not know why he is alive. The books say 4200 is not survivable. The books are the books. Victor is the Victor. The books are wrong or Victor is wrong and I am writing it down and I am not writing which because I do not know which and the not-knowing is the medicine I am practicing.

cases.symptoms: Day 40. Cumulative dose 380 mSv (estimated, occupational — repeated trips to ruins). Acute: none. Chronic: mild fatigue, occasional nausea. No epilation. No petechiae. Lymphocyte count 1.2 (low-normal).
cases.intervention: Reduce exposure: limit trips to 1 per week, duration under 4h. Dosimeter issued (see Requisition). Return for re-assessment Day 50.
cases.outcome: Stable. Occupational exposure within provisional limits.
cases.doctor_margin_note: She goes where the rest of us will not. She goes for the list. The list is the copper and the brass and the things we need. The dose is the cost of the list. I am writing the dose. I am writing the cost. The cost is the margin. The margin is where the doctor writes the cost of the things the shelter needs. The shelter needs the copper. The copper costs the Mira. I am writing the Mira.

cases.symptoms: Day 20. Shelter-wide baseline dosimetry. 147 persons assessed. Mean cumulative dose: 85 mSv (range 12-4200, skewed by acute cases). Background in shelter: 0.3 uSv/h (within safe limits).
cases.intervention: Continue monitoring. Repeat baseline Day 50. Flag any individual >250 mSv for individual follow-up.
cases.outcome: Population within provisional limits, excluding acute cases (see individual ledgers).
cases.doctor_margin_note: The mean is 85. The mean is a lie. The mean is the 85 that includes the 4200 and the 12 and the 12 is the child and the 4200 is the Victor and the mean is the number that hides them both. I am writing the mean because the form wants the mean. The mean is the form. The 12 and the 4200 are the margin. The margin is the doctor. The doctor is the 12 and the 4200 and not the 85.

cases.symptoms: Post-mortem, Day 33, approx 6h post-death. External: no trauma, no burns, no epilation. Internal: lungs bilaterally consolidated, lower lobes, purulent. Heart unremarkable. No other gross pathology. No culturing available.
cases.intervention: Cause of death: respiratory failure, secondary to infection (type undetermined). Contributing: aspiration event (river, Day 12). Treatment: broad-spectrum 2 courses, narrow 1 course. Outcome: not responsive.
cases.outcome: Deceased. Body to cold room. Burial Day 34, south plot, unmarked (per policy).
cases.doctor_margin_note: She did not respond to the narrow. I did not expect her to respond to the narrow. I gave her the narrow because the broad was for the strong. I wrote that decision down on Day 26. I am writing it down again here. The decision is the same decision. The lungs are the lungs. The lungs are the proof of the decision. The proof is in the margin. The margin is where the doctor writes the proof of the decisions the doctor made. I made the decision. The lungs are the proof. I am the doctor. I am writing.

cases.symptoms: Post-mortem, Day 95, approx 4h post-death. External: complete epilation, petechiae resolved (ante-mortem). Internal: sternal marrow cavity pale, gelatinous, fatty. No hematopoietic tissue identified. Spleen small, fibrotic. Lungs: mild fibrosis. No gross hemorrhage.
cases.intervention: Cause of death: pancytopenia and sepsis, secondary to acute radiation exposure (4200 mSv, Day 1). Survival: 95 days post-exposure.
cases.outcome: Deceased. Body to cold room. Burial Day 96, south plot, unmarked.
cases.doctor_margin_note: He lived 95 days. The books said he would die in 30. He lived 95. The books are the books. Victor was the Victor. The marrow is the proof. The marrow is the gelatinous fat and the pale and the nothing. The nothing is the proof. The proof is that the 4200 took the marrow and the marrow took the Victor and the Victor took 95 days to go and I am writing the 95 and I am writing the nothing and the nothing is the margin and the margin is the doctor and the doctor is tired.

cases.symptoms: Post-mortem, Day 70. External: cold, no trauma. Internal: no gross pathology. No signs of infection. Stomach empty. Muscle glycogen depleted.
cases.intervention: Cause of death: hypothermia, exposure. Contributing: malnutrition, dehydration. No radiation findings.
cases.outcome: Deceased. Body to cold room. Burial Day 71, south plot, unmarked.
cases.doctor_margin_note: He was old. He was cold. He was found by the road, the south road, the one the courier takes. He was not the courier. He was an old man. He was cold. The cold is the cause. The cold is the cause I write on the form. The form wants a cause. The cold is the cause. The old is the margin. The margin is where the doctor writes that the old die first in the cold and the cold is the cause and the old is the reason and the reason is the margin and the margin is the doctor.

cases.symptoms: Day 26. No improvement on broad. Temperature 38.8. Rales bilaterally, worse. Sputum purulent, now blood-tinged. Third case presenting (see med_treat_23).
cases.intervention: Decision: continue broad for cases 1 and 2 (the strong). Switch case 1 (river woman) to narrow, on trial, pending outcome. Hold reserve.
cases.doctor_margin_note: I am switching her to the narrow. I do not think the narrow will work. I am switching her because the broad is for the strong and she is not the strong and the strong are the two who carried her and I am making the bet on the strong and I am writing the bet and the bet is the narrow and the narrow is the bet and the bet is the margin and the margin is the doctor and the doctor is choosing and the choosing is the medicine and the medicine is the narrow and the narrow is not enough and I know it is not enough and I am giving it anyway because the broad is for the strong.

cases.symptoms: Day 26. Third case. Same ward, same presentation. Adult, previously well. Wet cough, temperature 38.5, rales right lower lobe.
cases.intervention: Begin broad-spectrum. Isolate (sheeted bay, with cases 1 and 2). Three cases now. The broad is for the three. The reserve is the reserve.
cases.doctor_margin_note: Three. I have three and I have ten courses and the math is the math and the math is not enough. I am treating the three with the broad and I am holding the reserve and the reserve is for the fourth and there will be a fourth and the fifth and the math is the math and the math is the margin and the margin is where the doctor writes that the math is not enough and the doctor is the math and the math is the doctor and we are both not enough.

cases.symptoms: Day 30. Narrow not effective. Temperature 39.0. Increasing respiratory distress. Cyanosis of nail beds. The narrow is not working. I knew the narrow would not work.
cases.intervention: Continue supportive care. Fluids. Position upright. No further antibiotics indicated — reserve held for the strong. Palliative.
cases.doctor_margin_note: I am writing 'palliative' for the first time. The word is the word. The word is the margin. The margin is the doctor admitting the narrow is not working and the broad is for the strong and the river woman is not the strong and the palliative is the medicine and the medicine is the comfort and the comfort is the hand and the hand is the nurse and the nurse is the one who is there when the doctor has nothing left to give. I have nothing left to give. The nurse has the hand. The hand is the medicine now.

cases.symptoms: Day 60. Victor awake, weak. Asked for water, drank. Asked about the sky again. I told him it was clearing. It is not clearing. The sky is the sky.
cases.intervention: Mouth care, hourly. Sips of water. Turned every 2h. Hand held. He held my hand back, weak.
cases.doctor_margin_note: He asked about the sky. I told him it was clearing. I am the nurse. I lie about the sky. The doctor writes the dose and the prognosis and the margin. I write the sky. The sky is my margin. The sky is the lie I tell the ones who are going. I tell them it is clearing. It is not clearing. I am the nurse. The nurse tells the sky. The doctor tells the dose. We are the two margins of the same patient and the patient is going and the sky is the lie and the dose is the truth and the patient hears the sky and not the dose and I am glad and I am sorry.

cases.symptoms: Day 20. Kolya's hand healed. He is using it. He drew me a picture with the healed hand. The picture is the sun. The sun has a face. The face is smiling. He gave it to me.
cases.intervention: Dressing discontinued. No further nursing indicated. Return to school.
cases.doctor_margin_note: He drew the sun with the hand I dressed. The hand is the medicine. The sun is the medicine. The medicine is the picture. I am the nurse and the nurse keeps the picture. I am keeping the picture. The picture is on the wall by my cot. The sun is smiling. The sun is not smiling. The sun is gone. The picture is smiling. The picture is the sun now. The picture is the only sun. I am the nurse and I keep the sun.

cases.symptoms: Day 33, 03:00. Restless. Breathing shallow. I sat with her. I held her hand. She did not hold back. She does not hold back. I held anyway.
cases.intervention: Mouth care. Forehead cool cloth. Hand held. Nothing else to give.
cases.doctor_margin_note: She died at four. I was there. The doctor was not. The doctor confirms at six. I confirm at four. The four is the nurse's. The six is the doctor's. The four is the hand. The six is the form. She did not have a name. I called her the river woman. The river woman is the name I gave her. The name is the margin. The margin is the nurse. The nurse names the ones who come without names. I named her. She died with the name I gave her. The river woman. I am the nurse. I name the dead. The naming is the medicine. The medicine is the name.

cases.symptoms: Frostbite, right foot, toes 2-4. White, hard, no sensation. Rewarming in progress (water bath, 38C). Pain on rewarming (good sign).
cases.intervention: Rewarm. Elevate. No rubbing. Watch for blistering. If blistering, do not debride. Dry dressing.
cases.outcome: Rewarming. Sensation returning to toes 2-3. Toe 4 uncertain.
cases.doctor_margin_note: The cupola is cold. I have written 'the cupola is cold' on every sentry intake this week. The cupola is always cold. The frostbite is the cupola. I am treating the cupola by treating the toes. The toes are the cupola. The cupola is the cold. I cannot treat the cold. I treat the toes. The toes are the margin. The margin is the nurse. The nurse treats the margin because the nurse cannot treat the cold.

cases.symptoms: Laceration, right forearm, 6cm, from fall in dark (see Incident Report IR-3-05). Clean wound, no foreign body. Knee contusion, no fracture.
cases.intervention: Clean with boiled water. Suture (3 stitches, nylon from kit). Dress. Tetanus status unknown — no prophylaxis available. Light duty 2 days.
cases.doctor_margin_note: He fell in the dark. The dark is the cause. The dark is not on the form. The form wants the cause. I wrote 'fall in dark.' The dark is the cause. The candles are the cause. The candles are not on the form. The candles are the margin. The margin is where the nurse writes that the dark is the cause and the candles are the cure and the cure is in the quartermaster's office and the cure is not in sub-level 3. I sewed the arm. The arm is the medicine. The dark is the disease.

cases.patient_name: Ward B Respiratory Cluster — Day 30 Report
cases.symptoms: Cluster of 3 respiratory cases, Ward B, Days 12-26. Index case: river woman (aspiration, Day 12). Secondary: carrier (Day 19), third case (Day 26). Consistent presentation: wet cough, rales, purulent sputum, fever. No culturing available. Clinical diagnosis: bacterial pneumonia, possible aspiration origin, secondary transmission suspected.
cases.intervention: Treatment: broad-spectrum (cases 2, 3), narrow (case 1, palliative). Isolation: sheeted bay, Ward B quarantine (see Quarantine Order). Outcome: case 1 deceased (Day 33), cases 2 and 3 recovered.
cases.outcome: Cluster contained. No new cases after Day 26. Quarantine lifted Day 40.
cases.doctor_margin_note: The cluster is contained. The word 'contained' is the word I am writing in the report. The report is the form. The form is the official. The official is the doctor who writes 'contained' and means 'three people got sick and one died and the others did not and I do not know why the others did not and the contained is the not-knowing and the not-knowing is the report and the report is the form and the form is the official and the official is the doctor and the doctor is tired and the doctor is writing 'contained' and the contained is the margin and the margin is the three and the one and the not-knowing.

cases.symptoms: Population 147. Mean weight loss since intake: 4.2kg (range 0-11). Mild deficiency signs: angular stomatitis (12 cases), glossitis (8), dry skin (widespread, non-specific). No frank deficiency disease (beriberi, pellagra, scurvy) observed. Children: growth stalling, no weight gain in 3 weeks.
cases.intervention: Recommend: maintain ration, prioritize protein for children and nursing mothers. Source fresh food (greenhouse, cold frame — see Farmer Petr). Supplement with wild forage if safe. Monitor children weight weekly.
cases.doctor_margin_note: The children are not growing. The children are not growing because the flour is the flour and the flour is at a number I am not going to write in the nutritional report because the nutritional report is the form and the form is the weight and the weight is the stalling and the stalling is the margin and the margin is the flour and the flour is the quartermaster and the quartermaster is the number and the number is the not-growing and the not-growing is the children and the children are the margin and the margin is the doctor.

cases.symptoms: Honey, topical, burn dressing, right hand. Daily. Day 7 of treatment.
cases.intervention: Applied to clean gauze, laid on burn, wrapped with linen. Tolerated. Child reports 'it tickles.'
cases.doctor_margin_note: The honey is the medicine. The honey is from the allotment, from the old hives, from before. The honey is the last of the honey. I am using the last of the honey on the boy's hand. The hand is the honey. The honey is the hand. I am using the last of the old world on the hand of the new world and the hand is healing and the honey is going and I am writing the honey going and the going is the margin and the margin is the nurse.

cases.symptoms: Day 90. Persistent fatigue. Weight 58kg (from 74 at intake). Lymphocyte count 0.6 (stable, low). No bleeding. No infection. Eating, small amounts. Sleeping, much. He is tired. He is always tired.
cases.intervention: Continue supportive. No specific therapy available. Rest. Nutrition. Comfort (see Nurse Anya notes).
cases.doctor_margin_note: He is declining. The decline is the 4200. The 4200 is the decline. The decline is slow. The slow is 90 days. 90 days is the margin. The margin is the doctor watching the slow and writing the slow and the slow is the medicine the doctor does not have and the medicine the doctor does not have is the watching and the watching is the margin and the margin is the doctor and the doctor is watching Victor and Victor is declining and I am writing it and I cannot stop it and I am writing it.

cases.symptoms: Day 95, 02:00. Victor awake. Asked for water, drank. Asked about the sky. I told him it was clearing. He smiled. He closed his eyes. He did not open them again.
cases.intervention: Mouth care. Hand held. He held my hand back, once, weak. Then not.
cases.doctor_margin_note: He smiled when I told him the sky was clearing. The sky is not clearing. The smile is the truth. The sky is the lie. The smile is the truth. I told him the lie and he gave me the truth and the truth is the smile and the smile is the margin and the margin is the nurse and the nurse is the one who tells the lie to get the truth and the truth is the smile and the smile is the last thing and I am the nurse and I have the smile and the smile is the medicine and the medicine is the lie and the lie is the sky and the sky is not clearing and the smile is.

cases.symptoms: Presents with insomnia, auditory complaints ('the vent hums like a choir'), decline in self-care. No organic cause identified on exam. Oriented, no psychosis. Exhausted.
cases.intervention: Reassurance. Quiet hours, earplugs if available (not available). Reduce night shifts if possible. Warm drink at night if available. Watch.
cases.doctor_margin_note: He hears the choir. I do not hear the choir. I hear the vent. The vent is the vent. He hears the choir. The choir is his vent. I cannot treat his vent. I can treat his sleep. The sleep is the medicine. The choir is the margin. The margin is the nurse who writes that the patient hears what the nurse does not and the nurse believes the patient and the nurse cannot help and the nurse writes it and the writing is the help and the help is the margin.

cases.symptoms: Day 44. Cumulative dose 12 mSv (low, sheltered since Day 1). Acute: none. Chronic: none. Growth: stalling (see Nutritional Report). Development: appropriate. The child is well. The child is the child.
cases.intervention: No intervention. Continue shelter. Monitor growth. The child is the measure of the shelter.
cases.doctor_margin_note: 12. The 12 is the child. The 12 is the lowest. The 12 is the number I am grateful for. The 12 is the margin. The margin is the doctor writing the lowest number and the lowest number is the child and the child is the shelter and the shelter is the 12 and the 12 is the reason. The reason is the child. The child is the reason. I am the doctor. I am writing the 12. The 12 is the child. The child is well. The child is the reason the doctor is the doctor.
